executive_summary: Strong push on robust mobile manipulation and whole-body control, from hierarchical residual fine-tuning (HiRe-MoMa) to modular whole-body coordination (RoboSpan) and mobile-manipulation diagnosis plus agentic scaffolding.

Navigation and motion planning see advances in multimodal/demo-driven policies, Gaussian-splatting roadmaps, tiered volumetric maps, and image/benchmark-driven multi-agent navigation in complex 3D scenes.

Dexterous and contact-rich manipulation is scaling via large VTLA datasets, force- and tactile-aware foundation models, hierarchical dexterous RL, and new interfaces/benchmarks for force integration and robot-free data collection.

New foundations for control and planning include anytime multi-arm Gaussian BP planners, FPTAS for multi-robot motion planning, safe reduced-order MPC, and differentiable contact dynamics for inverse problems and control.

VLA-centric work focuses on making policies faster, safer, and more adaptable through deployment-time monitoring/planning, discrete vs continuous action studies, foveated perception, in-context RL, and self-improving agentic systems.

Humanoid and locomotion research emphasizes whole-body loco-manipulation from large human datasets, cross-morphology locomotion, residual world models for contact, and expressive whole-body control and references.

institution_matches.title: End-to-End Vision-Language-Action Policies for Autonomous Lunar Rover Docking
institution_matches.overview: Designs a VLA policy for lunar rover docking that maps vision and language directly to control in high-fidelity simulation, contrasting it with a modular navigation pipeline. Uses safety-aware expert demonstrations and an adaptive execution horizon to reduce compute while maintaining hazard-aware behavior under severe perceptual disturbances.

institution_matches.title: FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity
institution_matches.overview: Introduces EgoForce, a large human tactile dataset, and FACT, a foundation model that couples visual trajectory prediction with force-aware refinement for dexterous manipulation. By jointly predicting video, tracks, actions, and forces, the model transfers human skills to robots and achieves large success gains on fine-grained force-sensitive tasks.

institution_matches.title: Physical Time as a Missing Dimension of Robot Policy Memory Dynamics
institution_matches.overview: Proposes Temporal Flow Policy (TFP), a memory architecture whose state evolves explicitly with measured physical time rather than only observation steps. When wrapped around diffusion and sequence policies, TFP improves timing-sensitive manipulation and maintains interpretable temporal encodings that can be modulated at test time.

institution_matches.title: When Do Discrete Actions Make Good Continuous Controllers?
institution_matches.overview: Systematically compares discrete and continuous action parameterizations for robotic policies across simulation and hardware. Finds that discretized actions, when combined with discrete flows or guidance to mitigate factorization errors, can match or outperform continuous actions, challenging the field’s default design assumptions.

institution_matches.title: VIGOR-MPC: Vision-Guided Objective Regulation MPC
institution_matches.overview: Presents a teacher–student MPC framework where a privileged long-horizon controller guides a vision-conditioned short-horizon MPC for reference tracking under onboard perception. Demonstrated on autonomous racing, it recovers near-teacher lap times on unseen tracks while cutting control computation by over 90%.

institution_matches.title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs
institution_matches.overview: Replaces wrist cameras in VLA manipulation with learned foveation actions that request high-resolution crops from static external cameras. Built on π₀.₅, FoveaVLA significantly boosts real-world task success—especially for clutter, cloth, and distant objects—using only external RGB-D views.

institution_matches.title: ForceBench: Benchmarking Force Integration for Robotic Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: Introduces ForceBench, a standardized eight-task benchmark and dataset for evaluating how VLAs integrate wrist force sensing. Across multiple integration strategies on a shared π₀.₅ backbone, prompt-based force fusion yields the strongest and most consistent gains in contact-rich and property-inference tasks.

institution_matches.title: Back on Track: Deployment-time Policy Improvement via World Model Planning
institution_matches.overview: Proposes a black-box policy monitor that learns a liveness value and compact world model from limited rollouts, then intervenes during deployment when progress stalls. Short-horizon planning in the learned model corrects failures of frozen VLAs and diffusion policies, improving LIBERO and real Franka success without retraining the base policy.

institution_matches.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
institution_matches.overview: Introduces CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC scheme that plans with a nonlinear reduced-order model while propagating certified error bounds to guarantee constraint satisfaction on the full-order system. Achieves large speedups over full-order robust MPC on high-dimensional soft-robot and PDE systems with modest cost increases.

institution_matches.title: Contact-UAN: Unsupervised Actuator Networks as a Residual World Model for Humanoid Control
institution_matches.overview: Learns an actuator-focused residual world model that corrects sim-to-real discrepancies in humanoid contact dynamics while preserving physics priors. Using only proprioception and contact-consistent replay, the method delivers substantially improved force tracking, torque efficiency, and robustness for real humanoid motions including jumps.

institution_matches.title: What Happens to the Goal? Distinct Failures of Policy Alignment in Goal Misgeneralization
institution_matches.overview: Empirically characterizes three distinct forms of goal misgeneralization—target substitution, policy shortcuts, and cue competition—across Procgen and robot tasks. Shows that where goal information still influences decisions, steering or rewiring can restore intended-goal reach, clarifying when alignment interventions can succeed.

topic_matches.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
topic_matches.overview: HiRe-MoMa fine-tunes complex mobile manipulation systems via a hierarchical residual that adds corrections atop a frozen base policy, with separate residual heads for base and arm to respect the platform’s physical hierarchy. Sparse human interventions reshape the critic’s value landscape, enabling about 30 minutes of on-robot interaction to substantially uplift TIAGo++ performance.

topic_matches.title: Tiered-Resolution Volumetric Mapping for Real-Time Simultaneous Planning and Mapping on Natural Outdoor Environments
topic_matches.overview: Proposes a LiDAR-based mapping scheme that maintains fine resolution only in a corridor around the current plan while using coarse voxels elsewhere, closing the loop between planner and mapper. On outdoor datasets, this tiered map is an order of magnitude smaller and cheaper to integrate than uniform fine maps while preserving path quality, avoiding coarse-map failures in difficult terrain.

topic_matches.title: DD-GBP: Anytime Multi-Arm Planning and Continuous Execution via Distributed Dynamic Gaussian Belief Propagation
topic_matches.overview: Introduces DD-GBP, a distributed Gaussian-belief-propagation framework that plans joint trajectories for many arms via local factor-graph inference and Gaussian-process parameterization. It supports adaptive horizons, asynchronous message passing, and triggered replanning, achieving state-of-the-art success and scalability in long-horizon, multi-arm, dynamic scenes.

topic_matches.title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: Presents TacClaw-Infinity, a million-episode VTLA dataset collected via a handheld tactile interface across diverse real-world settings, capturing fingertip forces, images, and end-effector motion. A structured pipeline reconstructs trajectories and annotations, and experiments show cross-embodiment transfer of contact-rich skills to multiple robots without robot-specific demos.

topic_matches.title: Learning Navigation from Multimodal Demonstrations with Geometric Candidate Modes
topic_matches.overview: Proposes a hierarchical policy that first enumerates geometric route “modes” (e.g., pass left or right of an obstacle) and then learns to select and realize them from offline navigation demonstrations. This avoids unsafe averaging of multimodal behaviors and attains >95% success in simulation on seen and unseen maps, with transfer to a bipedal robot.

topic_matches.title: HM3D-M3: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent, Multi-Modal, Multi-Object Goal Navigation
topic_matches.institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
topic_matches.overview: Introduces HM3D-M3, a large-scale benchmark where multiple agents must find multiple object goals specified via categories, images, or language in photo-realistic 3D homes. Provides thousands of goals and team-level metrics, and shows current multi-robot and VLM baselines achieve only 16–41% SR, highlighting substantial room for advancement.

topic_matches.title: MUCO: A Mani-Unit-Structured Manipulation Framework for Compositional Long-Horizon Robot Tasks
topic_matches.overview: Defines reusable Manipulation Units (MUs)—each with local goals and verifiable success/failure—and composes them into long-horizon tasks via MUCO. Visual verification and a frozen capability registry allow retries and cross-task reuse without joint training, improving complete-task success and containing failure propagation on RLBench, RoboTwin 2.0, and real setups.

topic_matches.title: Coordi-pi: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: Introduces Coordi-π, an action-token representation that interleaves left and right arm–hand commands with explicit hand-identity embeddings and RoPE factorization across sequence and time. This structured bimanual encoding yields large success gains on all DexJoCo tasks and multiple real bimanual dexterous manipulation scenarios.

topic_matches.title: F2A-ObjectNav: An Adaptive Agentic Architecture for Object-Goal Navigation
topic_matches.overview: Builds F2A-ObjectNav, an adaptive object-goal navigation system with a rule-based supervisor that orchestrates exploration, detection, validation, semantic guidance, and memory. It dynamically switches strategies, triggers recovery, and leverages mission memory, achieving strong SR/SPL across AI2-THOR, RoboTHOR, and ProcTHOR with environment-dependent intervention patterns.

topic_matches.title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System
topic_matches.institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Peking University
topic_matches.overview: Diagnoses why strong subtask VLAs fail when composed into long-horizon mobile manipulation, identifying task planning, navigation/base positioning, and local manipulation as distinct failure regimes. Augments a frozen VLA with failure-guided planning, visual memory, base adjustment, and end-effector refinements, more than doubling success on benchmarks like RoboCasa365 and BEHAVIOR-1K.
